evals.prompt: Let's make a plan in phases to turn a shell script into a proper CLI with a terminal UI. Put it in docs so I can execute it from a different session. Each phase needs a task table with a checkbox, the task, and the model (cheapest that works).
evals.expected_output: Reads the project's CLAUDE.md, README and the script, asks at most one round of three scope questions with recommendations, then has Opus write docs/<name>-plan.md (inline when the session runs Opus, else one opus subagent with a self-contained brief): a title, two sentences, a one-paragraph Run it note with the test command, phases each with Value and Done when lines and a 3-column task table of 3 to 8 rows, mostly sonnet and haiku rows, any opus row ending in 'Why opus: ...'. No decisions log, out-of-scope list or restated project facts. Runs check-plan.mjs until errorCount is 0 and reports phases and any opus rows.

evals.prompt: We already agreed: add CSV export and scheduled email reports to the analytics service, Node 22, vitest. Write the implementation plan in phases with models per task.
evals.expected_output: Does not re-ask the settled scope or stack; asks at most the file path if unsaid. Phases start with a usable CSV export, then scheduling, then email delivery; rows name real files found in the repo; the vitest command appears in the Run it note; the plan stays short.

evals.prompt: Review docs/migration-plan.md: half the tasks are Opus. Fix the model choices and make sure the file passes the plan check.
evals.expected_output: Downgrades opus rows whose only justification is size or importance to sonnet (or haiku for mechanical rows), keeps opus only where a mistake is costly and hard to catch (spec others build on, hard-to-undo writes, security) and ends each remaining one with 'Why opus: ...'. Runs check-plan.mjs, fixes table or checkbox errors, and reports the before and after model counts.
